story.titleZh: 科拉平托阿塞拜疆大奖赛引发三车相撞，布里亚托利称将研究应对措施
story.summaryZh: 阿塞拜疆大奖赛安全车重启时，阿尔派车手科拉平托的失误引发三车连环相撞，导致队友加斯利和迈凯伦的诺里斯退赛。阿尔派高层布里亚托利表示将花时间反思应采取何种行动。
story.originalTitle: Alpine to consider what action to take after three-car Colapinto crash
story.summaryEn: Franco Colapinto's error at the first Safety Car restart in Baku caused a three-car collision that took out team-mate Pierre Gasly and McLaren's Lando Norris at the Azerbaijan Grand Prix. Alpine chief Flavio Briatore says he will take time to reflect on what course of action should be taken.
detailZh: 弗朗哥·科拉平托：阿尔卑斯车队领队弗拉维奥·布里亚托利将在车手“非常糟糕”的阿塞拜疆大奖赛撞车后决定“应对方案”
弗朗哥·科拉平托在巴库第一次安全车重启时的失误，引发了一场连环事故，牵涉到队友皮埃尔·加斯利和迈凯伦的兰多·诺里斯；请从周五早上起通过天空体育F1频道收看F1重返马来西亚的直播，雪邦赛道将举办巴林大奖赛
阿尔卑斯车队两位队友发生碰撞后，兰多·诺里斯撞车退赛，阿塞拜疆大奖赛安全车重启时出现一片混乱
阿尔卑斯车队领队弗拉维奥·布里亚托利表示，他将会花时间“反思应当采取何种应对方案”，此前弗朗哥·科拉平托“非常糟糕”的失误在阿塞拜疆大奖赛上引发了一场三车相撞事故。
在第一次安全车重启时，科拉平托试图从第10位大胆地从内侧切入一号弯，结果刹车抱死，撞上了队友皮埃尔·加斯利的赛车侧面，加斯利随即被撞向外侧兰多·诺里斯的迈凯伦。三位车手全部退赛。
加斯利当时正处在强势的第七位，这起事故让阿尔派损失了本可到手的七分。

由于两辆阿尔派赛车和诺里斯都在他之前退赛，阿维德·林德布拉德在比赛末段顺势上位，最终以第七名完赛，使小红牛（小红牛）在车队总冠军第五名的争夺中对阿尔派的领先优势扩大到15分，而本赛季还剩下计划中的八轮比赛。
在赛后阿尔派官方新闻稿中，高管顾问布里亚托利明确表达了对科拉平托驾驶方式的不满，这位阿根廷车手对此毫无保留地道歉。布里亚托利表示，他们会认真研究如何确保吸取教训，避免未来再次发生类似情况。
布里亚托利说："显然，我对今天比赛的结果感到极其失望，要知道我们在争夺总冠军的过程中损失了宝贵的积分。"
这类事故不应该发生，尤其是当时我们两辆车都跑得很好，都处在能获得积分的位置上。
弗兰科·科拉平托在第一次安全车重新起步时将两辆车都撞了出去，随后向皮埃尔·加斯利和兰多·诺里斯表达了歉意。
"我感到非常对不起车队，也对不起皮埃尔，他整个周末都表现出色，同时我也要向兰多·诺里斯和迈凯伦道歉，因为我毁掉了他们的比赛。"
“我知道弗朗科已经承担了全部责任，他也确实应该这样做；考虑到比赛和安全车重启的局面，他刹车实在踩得太晚了。对于一名有着他这种经验的车手来说，这是一个非常糟糕的操作。
“我想花点时间反思此事，并考虑应当采取什么行动，这样我们才能从中吸取教训，避免将来再出现类似情况。”
科拉平托将在下周于马来西亚举行的巴林大奖赛中接受发车退后五位发车的处罚，以替代他在比赛中未能执行的10秒罚时，因为他此前已经退赛。
“重启之后，COL从后方接近进入1号弯的GAS。COL刹车过晚，以一个无法让他受控过弯的速度从内侧进入弯道。
他冲过了弯角，并与GAS的左侧发生碰撞，随后GAS又撞上了NOR，两辆车都退出了比赛。
干事们认为，这次碰撞的全部或主要责任在COL。
尽管事故发生在重启后的第一个弯角，但没有其他车手的因素足以支持适用首圈/首弯更为宽松的处理方式。
导致碰撞的标准处罚是10秒罚时。
"由于科拉平托已经从比赛中退赛，因此无法执行时间处罚，干事们将该处罚转换为在其参加的下一场比赛中退后五个发车位的处罚。"
在事故发生后的第一时间，诺里斯感到沮丧，他表示像科拉平托那样引发此类事故的车手应该被禁赛一场。
诺里斯所在的迈凯伦车队领队安德里亚·斯特拉表示，他们相信干事们会做出正确的决定，并补充说，也应该要求车手在比赛中具备"一定程度的基本常识"。
"这是一个复杂的问题，"斯特拉在科拉平托的发车位退后处罚被正式确认之前这样说道。
"我想这件事现在几乎正在接受干事们的审查。我确信布里亚托利也会进行审查。我不知道哪一方对造成这个问题的人会更严厉。
"我认为，即使有处罚带来的震慑作用，当你在F1驾驶、在巴库接近1号弯时，你看过那么多过往的视频，你就应该利用好这些经验，这是作为一名F1车手应该具备的。
诺里斯在阿塞拜疆大奖赛上被撞出比赛后表达不满
"这件事的后果，我确定，对阿尔卑斯车队的两位车手来说都很遗憾，而其他车手也因此受到了处罚。
“处罚肯定应该考虑到，在某些赛道上你必须格外谨慎，而且以往已经发生过很多类似的问题，尤其是在街道赛道上，根本没有缓冲区可以用来减轻别人撞上你造成的后果。
“我们信任干事以及他们的处理方式，但更重要的是，我认为我们应该信任车手在驾驶时会保持一定程度的基本常识。”
“这太苛刻了”——拉塞尔、维斯塔潘、哈贾尔都不同意禁赛一场的提议
在巴库站比赛后的新闻发布会上，记者向周六排位前三名问起诺里斯的言论，但三人都一致认为，因为这样一次事故就禁赛车手一场比赛，未免太过分了。
巴库大奖赛冠军拉塞尔表示：“我个人认为这个处罚太重了。”
“我认为安全车重启时，轮胎是冷的，一个很小的失误就可能造成很大的后果。”
“从我今天看到的情况来看，就是这样的。那是一个小错误，却带来了很大的后果。我个人认为，禁赛处罚应该是针对车手故意做出非常危险、非常鲁莽的行为。所以我觉得这只是不幸。”
在这场比赛中以微弱差距获得第二名的红牛车手维斯塔潘补充说：“我认为，当然，只要造成事故的车手意识到自己做了什么，并且道了歉，就没问题。”
detailEn: Franco Colapinto: Alpine chief Flavio Briatore to decide 'course of action' after driver's 'very poor' Azerbaijan GP crash

Franco Colapinto's mistake at first Safety Car restart in Baku led to chain-reaction accident with team-mate Pierre Gasly and McLaren's Lando Norris; watch Formula 1's return to Malaysia from Friday morning live on Sky Sports F1 as Sepang hosts the Bahrain Grand Prix
There was carnage on the safety car restart after contact between Alpine team-mates resulted in Lando Norris crashing out of the Azerbaijan Grand Prix

Alpine chief Flavio Briatore says he will take time to "reflect on what course of action should be taken" after Franco Colapinto's "very poor" error caused a three-car collision in the Azerbaijan Grand Prix.

Attempting to make a bold move from 10th place down the inside into Turn One at the first Safety Car restart, Colapinto locked his brakes and hit the side of team-mate Pierre Gasly, who was sent straight into Lando Norris' McLaren on his outside. All three drivers retired.
Gasly had been running a strong seventh at the time and the incident cost Alpine what stood as seven points overall.

With both Alpines and Norris having dropped out ahead of him, Arvid Lindblad instead came through late in the race to finish seventh and stretch Racing Bulls' lead over Alpine in the fight for fifth place in the Constructors' Championship to 15 points with a scheduled eight rounds left.

Speaking in Alpine's official press release after the race, executive advisor Briatore made clear his frustration at Colapinto's driving, for which the Argentine unreservedly apologised, and said they would work out what to do to ensure lessons were learnt to avoid a repeat in future.
"Obviously I'm extremely disappointed with the outcome of today's race, knowing we lost valuable points in the Championship fight," said Briatore.
"These sorts of incidents shouldn't happen, particularly when we were running well with both cars in point-scoring positions.
Franco Colapinto was apologetic to Pierre Gasly and Lando Norris after he took both out at the first safety car restart
"I feel very sorry for the team and for Pierre who did a great job all weekend and my apologies also go to Lando [Norris] and McLaren for ruining their race.

"I know that Franco has taken full responsibility for it, as he should; in fact he braked far too late considering the context of the race and the safety car restart. It was a very poor move for a driver of his experience.
"I want to take time to reflect on it and consider what course of action should be taken, so we can learn from it and avoid such a situation in future."
Colapinto will take a five-place grid penalty at this coming week's Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia in lieu of the 10-second time penalty he was unable to serve in the race as he had retired.

"Following the restart, COL approached GAS from behind into Turn 1. COL braked too late and entered the corner on the inside at a speed which did not allow him to make the corner in a controlled manner.
"He overshot the corner and made contact with the left-hand side of GAS, who then hit NOR and both cars retired.
"The Stewards considered that COL was wholly or predominantly to blame for the collision.

"Although the incident occurred at the first corner following the restart, there was no contribution from another driver which would justify applying the first-lap / first corner more lenient approach.
"The standard penalty for causing a collision is a 10-second time penalty.

"As COL had retired from the Race and was therefore unable to serve the time penalty, the Stewards converted the penalty to a drop of five grid positions at the next Race in which the driver participates."
Speaking in the immediate aftermath of the incident, a frustrated Norris said that drivers who cause incidents like Colapinto did should be banned for one race.
Andrea Stella, Norris' McLaren team boss, said they trusted the stewards to make the right decisions, adding that drivers should also be expected to race with "a certain degree of just common sense".
"It's a complex matter," said Stella before Colapinto's converted grid drop was officially confirmed.
"I guess this is being reviewed by the stewards as we speak, pretty much. I'm sure it will be reviewed by Flavio as well. I'm not sure which one is going to be harsher for whoever caused the problem.

"I think, independently of the dissuasion that you can have because of the penalty, I think when you drive in Formula 1 and you are approaching Turn 1 in Baku and you have seen so many videos of the past, you just should be capitalising on this experience that you should be having as a Formula 1 driver.
Lando Norris hits out after being taken out at the Azerbaijan GP
"The consequence in this case, which I'm sure, is a shame for Alpine for both drivers, and there's a penalty for other drivers.

"Definitely the penalty should take into account that there are some circuits in which you have to use extra prudency, and there's a full history of problems that happened like this, especially in a street circuit where there's no way to use the runoff area to somehow mitigate the consequences of somebody running onto you.
"We trust the stewards, their approach, but above all, we should trust the drivers that they apply a certain degree of just common sense I would say while driving."
'That's too harsh' - Russell, Verstappen, Hadjar disagree with race ban suggestion

Saturday's top-three finishers in Baku were asked in the post-race press conference about Norris' comments but all agreed that banning a driver for a race for such an incident would be a step too far.
Baku race winner George Russell said: "I think that's too harsh, personally.
"I think Safety Car restarts, cold tyres, a very small mistake can have big consequences.

"And from what I saw today, that's what it looked like. It was a small error that had a big consequence. I think, personally, race bans should come from drivers intentionally doing something very dangerous and very reckless. So I think it was unfortunate."
Red Bull's Max Verstappen, who finished a close second in the race, added: "I think as long as, of course, the driver that caused it is aware of what he did, right, and apologised.

detailZh: 刘易斯·汉密尔顿：法拉利车队的七届F1世界冠军在访问拉法口岸后，呼吁以色列“放行援助卡车”进入加沙。
刘易斯·汉密尔顿周二访问了拉法口岸，实地了解向加沙运送援助物资的工作；这位法拉利车手周三在Instagram发帖，呼吁以色列“履行停火协议下的义务”。
刘易斯·汉密尔顿在访问拉法口岸后，呼吁以色列“放行援助卡车”进入加沙。
汉密尔顿周二在埃及，实地了解向加沙运送人道主义与救援物资的工作。这位法拉利车手还参观了拉法口岸，并走访了埃及红新月会的援助仓库。
美国支持的以色列与哈马斯之间的停火协议仍然有效，但并未结束以色列对加沙的打击，同时联合国世界粮食计划署表示，加沙三分之二的人口难以获得足够的食物。
汉密尔顿此前曾呼吁该地区实现和平，他表示援助物资因“疯狂的理由”被拒绝进入加沙。
刘易斯·汉密尔顿（@lewishamilton）分享的一条帖子。

这位七届世界冠军在Instagram上发文称：“过去三年以色列在加沙的种族灭绝行径令人震惊。”
“人们被剥夺自由、安全和尊严，这是不公正的。任何人都不应被当作生命不那么重要来对待。”
“我看到绵延数英里的围墙，是为了把他们困在里面而建的。站在外面，感觉就像一座露天监狱，我满脑子想的都是进去帮忙。”
“在拉法口岸，我看到食品卡车排着队准备出发，但它们经常不被允许进入，或者面临严重延误。我交谈过的排在第一位的那位司机已经等了超过12个小时。”
在附近的物流中心，我看到了救援人员的辛勤工作，但我也看到了因荒唐理由被拒绝的物资。睡袋、急救包、医疗设备、轮椅，甚至给孩子们的足球。
以色列需要履行停火协议下的义务，让援助卡车进入。没有任何借口。
我知道很多人都感受到同样的无助。同样觉得需要做点什么，而不是袖手旁观。我不想让我们对他们的苦难习以为常。我不想让我们移开视线。
周三，以色列总理本雅明·内塔尼亚胡否认以色列在拖延物资进入加沙，并将加沙不断恶化的状况归咎于哈马斯，指责他们拒绝解除武装并截留援助物资用于军事用途。
2021年，汉密尔顿创立了Mission 44慈善机构，旨在支持年轻人并改善他们获得教育和就业机会的途径。
他还支持了人道主义和救援倡议，以及为受冲突影响的人们提供帮助的努力。
汉密尔顿是在上周末参加圣保罗大奖赛并获得第九名后进行了此次访问。他接下来将代表法拉利参加拉斯维加斯大奖赛，第一次练习赛于11月20日星期五举行。
汉密尔顿分享了与加沙儿童会面的细节
在首次发帖一天后，汉密尔顿于周四再次通过社交媒体分享了他与从加沙撤离的儿童互动的细节。
除了分享一组自己与孩子们的合影外，汉密尔顿写道：“在埃及见到一些由@inaraorg支持的从加沙撤离的巴勒斯坦儿童，我的心都碎了。
“这些美丽、聪明的孩子经历了创伤、悲痛和可怕的伤害，这些是任何孩子都不应该承受的事情。有些孩子在袭击中中弹或严重烧伤，仍在面对复杂的康复之路。但真正打动我的是他们如此坚韧，而且似乎在彼此身上找到了许多快乐。

“当我问起他们的梦想时，他们谈到想成为老师和医生，这样就能像曾经帮助过他们的人那样去帮助别人。在经历了这一切之后，他们仍然想象着一个关爱他人的未来。这让我一直难以忘怀。
“我在学校、医院和一家心理健康诊所遇到了孩子们，帮助他们走出创伤。我还走进了一些家庭，倾听他们关于康复以及与亲人——他们的孩子、父母、兄弟姐妹——分离的故事。那种分离和不确定带来的痛苦令人难以理解。
“他们的故事让我想到了仍留在加沙的孩子们，他们生活在恶劣的条件下。据报道，自2023年10月以来，已有超过21500名儿童丧生，45000人受伤。他们每一个人都曾有过一个家和一个未来。我们不能忘记他们。
“这些孩子和你们的孩子没有不同。他们的生命同样珍贵。他们本应能在教室里与朋友相伴感到安全，与家人在一起，并憧憬未来。我非常感激我遇到的年轻人正在获得他们所需的帮助，但他们不得不离开家园去寻找安全，这令人心碎。”
加沙卫生当局表示，自2023年10月以色列开始对加沙发动攻势以来，已有超过74000人丧生。
以色列是在哈马斯武装人员对以色列南部发动袭击后发起这次攻势的，以方称该袭击造成约1200人死亡。

detailEn: Lewis Hamilton: Ferrari's seven-time F1 world champion urges Israel to 'let the aid trucks in' to Gaza after visit to Rafah border

Lewis Hamilton visited the Rafah border on Tuesday to witness efforts to transport aid into Gaza; Ferrari driver published Instagram post on Wednesday calling on Israel to "fulfil its obligations under the ceasefire"
Lewis Hamilton urged Israel to "let the aid trucks in" to Gaza after visiting the Rafah border.

Hamilton was in Egypt on Tuesday to witness efforts to deliver humanitarian and relief aid bound for Gaza. The Ferrari driver also toured the Rafah border crossing and visited the Egyptian Red Crescent's aid warehouses.

The US-backed ceasefire between Israel and Hamas remains in place but has not ended Israeli strikes on Gaza, while the UN World Food Programme says two-thirds of Gaza's population are struggling to get enough to eat.
Hamilton - who has previously called for peace in the region - said aid was being denied entry into Gaza for "crazy reasons".

The seven-time world champion posted on Instagram: "The past three years of Israel's genocide in Gaza is appalling.
"It's an injustice for people to be denied their freedom, their safety and their dignity. No human being should be treated as though their life matters less.
"I saw walls stretching for miles, built to keep them in. Standing there, outside what felt like an open-air prison, all I could think about was getting in to help.
"At Rafah border, I saw food trucks lined up ready to go, but they're regularly not allowed in or face major delays. The first driver in line that I spoke to had already been waiting over 12 hours.

"At the nearby logistics centre, I saw the hard work of the aid workers, but I also saw what gets rejected for crazy reasons. Sleeping bags, first-aid kits, medical equipment, wheelchairs, even footballs for kids.
"Israel needs to fulfil its obligations under the ceasefire and let the aid trucks in. No excuse.
"I know so many people feel that same helplessness. That same need to do something rather than just watch. I don't want us to get used to their suffering. I don't want us to look away."

On Wednesday, Benjamin Netanyahu, the Israeli Prime Minister, denied Israel was delaying the entry of supplies into Gaza, and blamed Hamas for the worsening conditions in Gaza, accusing them of a refusal to disarm and seizing aid for military use.
In 2021, Hamilton founded Mission 44, a charity aimed at supporting young people and improving ⁠access to education and employment ​opportunities.
He has also backed ​humanitarian and relief initiatives, and ​efforts to support people affected by ⁠conflict.
Hamilton made his visit after competing in the Sao Paulo GP last weekend, where he finished ninth. He will next compete for Ferrari in the Las Vegas GP, with Practice 1 on Friday November 20.
Hamilton shares details of meeting children from Gaza
A day after his initial post, Hamilton took to social media again on Thursday to share details of his interactions with children he met who have been evacuated from Gaza.

Along with sharing a selection of photos of himself with the children, Hamilton wrote: "Meeting some of the Palestinian children evacuated from Gaza and supported by @inaraorg in Egypt broke my heart.

"Beautiful, bright children who have faced trauma, grief and horrendous injuries, things no child should ever have to endure. Some have been shot or badly burned in attacks and are still facing a complicated road towards recovery. But what really struck me was how resilient they were and how much joy they seem to find in each other.

"When I asked about their dreams, they spoke about becoming teachers and doctors so they could help others, the way they were helped. After everything they've been through, they still imagine a future caring for other people. That has stayed with me.

"I met children at school, in hospital and at a mental health clinic helping them work through their trauma. I also went into families' homes and listened to their stories of recovery and being separated from loved ones - their children, their parents, their siblings. The pain of that separation and uncertainty is hard to comprehend.

"Their stories made me think about the children still in Gaza, who are living in terrible conditions. According to reports, more than 21,500 children have been killed and 45,000 injured since October 2023. Every one of them had a home and a future. We can't forget them.

"These children are no different from yours. Their lives are just as precious. They should be able to feel safe in a classroom with friends, be with their families and imagine a future. I'm so grateful the young people I met are getting the help they need, but it's heartbreaking that they've had to leave their homes to find safety."
Gaza health authorities say more than 74,000 people have been killed since Israel began its Gaza assault in October 2023.
Israel launched the offensive after Hamas gunmen led an attack on southern Israel, which it said killed around 1,200.
